response.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x.`ANA Pattern` = 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL), AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Patients with no examination records at all count as having none with ANA Pattern 'S', so they are included. Their average is NULL and they sort last. Examination rows with a NULL ANA Pattern are not 'S', so they do not exclude the patient.
The comparison to 'S' is an exact, case-sensitive match on the whole value. Patterns such as 'S.P' or 'P.S' are different values and do not exclude the patient.

alternatives.interpretation: Only patients who have at least one examination record are considered, so patients with no examinations are excluded.
